Directions：In this section^ you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Meaning Is Healthier Than Happiness
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中^您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡上标记相应的字母来回答问题 2. 意义比幸福更健康

paragraphs.sourceText: A) For at least the last decade, the happiness craze has been building. In the last three months alone, over 1 000 books on happiness were released on Amazon, including Happy Money, Happy-People-Pills For All, and, for those just starting out, Happiness for Beginners.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 至少在过去十年里，幸福热潮一直在兴起。仅在过去三个月，亚马逊就发布了 1000 多本有关幸福的书籍，其中包括《快乐金钱》、《快乐人民药丸》以及针对刚刚起步的人的《初学者的幸福》。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) One of the consistent claims of books like these is that happiness is associated with all sorts of good life outcomes, including—most promisingly —good health. Many studies have noted the connection between a happy mind and a healthy body —the happier we are, the better health outcomes we seem to have. In an overview of 150 studies on this topic, researchers put it like this：“Inductions of well-being lead to healthy functioning, and inductions of ill-being lead to compromised health.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B）此类书籍的一致主张之一是，幸福与各种良好的生活成果相关，其中最有希望的是良好的健康。许多研究都指出了快乐的心灵和健康的身体之间的联系——我们越快乐，我们的健康状况似乎就越好。在对有关这一主题的 150 项研究的概述中，研究人员这样说道：“幸福的诱发会带来健康的功能，而不幸的诱发会导致健康受损。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C) But a new study, just published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) challenges the rosy picture. Happiness may not be as good for the body as researchers thought. It might even be bad.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 但刚刚发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》(PNAS) 上的一项新研究对这一美好前景提出了挑战。幸福可能并不像研究人员想象的那样对身体有益。甚至可能很糟糕。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) D) Of course, it’s important to first define Happiness. A few months ago, I wrote a piece called “There’s More to Life Than Being Happy” about a psychology study that dug into what happiness really means to people. It specifically explored the difference between a meaningful life and a happy life.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）D）当然，首先定义幸福很重要。几个月前，我写了一篇名为《生活不仅仅是幸福》的文章，内容涉及一项心理学研究，该研究深入探讨了幸福对人们的真正含义。它专门探讨了有意义的生活和幸福的生活之间的区别。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) It seems strange that there would be a difference at all. But the researchers, who looked at a large sample of people over a month-long period, found that happiness is associated with selfish “taking” behavior and that having a sense of meaning in life is associated with selfless “giving” behavior.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 会有什么不同似乎很奇怪。但研究人员在长达一个月的时间里对大量人群进行了观察，发现幸福与自私的“索取”行为有关，而拥有生活的意义感则与无私的“给予”行为有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) “Happiness without meaning characterizes a relatively shallow, self-absorbed or even selfish life, in which things go well, needs and desires are easily satisfied, and complicated relationships are avoided”, the authors of the study wrote. “If anything, pure happiness is linked to not helping others in need.” While being happy is about feeling good, meaning is derived from contributing to others or to society in a bigger way. As Roy Baumeister, one of the researchers, told me, “Partly what we do as human beings is to take care of others and contribute to others. This makes life meaningful but it does not necessarily make us happy. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: F）“没有意义的幸福是一种相对肤浅、自我陶醉甚至自私的生活，在这种生活中一切都很顺利，需要和欲望很容易得到满足，并且避免复杂的关系”，该研究的作者写道。 “如果说有什么不同的话，那就是纯粹的幸福与不帮助有需要的人有关。”虽然快乐是指感觉良好，但意义却来自于为他人或社会做出更大的贡献。正如研究人员之一罗伊·鲍迈斯特（Roy Baumeister）告诉我的那样，“我们作为人类所做的部分事情就是照顾他人并为他人做出贡献。这让生活变得有意义，但并不一定能让我们快乐。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The new PNAS study also sheds light on the difference between meaning and happiness, but on the biological level. Barbara Fredrickson, a psychological researcher at the University of North Carolina- Chapel Hill, and Steve Cole, a genetics and psychiatry(精神病学) researcher at UCLA, examined the self-reported levels of happiness and meaning in 80 research subjects.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 新的 PNAS 研究还揭示了意义和幸福之间的差异，但是在生物学层面上。北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校的心理学研究员芭芭拉·弗雷德里克森（Barbara Fredrickson）和加州大学洛杉矶分校的遗传学和精神病学研究员史蒂夫·科尔（Steve Cole）检查了 80 名研究对象自我报告的幸福感和意义感水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Happiness was defined, as in the earlier study, by feeling good. The researchers measured happiness by asking subjects questions like “How often did you feel happy?' “How often did you feel interested in life?” and “How often did you feel satisfied?” The more strongly people endorsed these measures of “hedonic (享乐主义的）well-being，” or pleasure, the higher they scored on happiness.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 正如之前的研究一样，幸福的定义是感觉良好。研究人员通过询问受试者诸如“你多久感到快乐一次？”等问题来衡量幸福感。 “你有多少次对生活感到感兴趣？”以及“您多久感到满意一次？”人们越强烈地支持这些“享乐主义的幸福”或快乐的衡量标准，他们的幸福得分就越高。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Meaning was defined as an orientation to something bigger than the self. They measured meaning by asking questions like “How often did you feel that your life has a sense of direction or meaning to it?” and “How often did you feel that you had something to contribute to society?” The more people endorsed these measures of “eudaimonic (幸福论的）well-being”-or, simply put, virtue —the more meaning they felt in life.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 意义被定义为对比自我更大的事物的定位。他们通过询问诸如“你有多少次感觉到你的生活有方向感或意义？”之类的问题来衡量意义。以及“您有多少次觉得自己可以为社会做出贡献？”越多的人赞同这些“幸福论的幸福”——或者简单地说，美德——的衡量标准，他们就越能感受到生活的意义。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) After noting the sense of meaning and happiness that each subject had, Fredrickson and Cole, with their research colleagues, looked at the ways certain genes expressed themselves in each of the participants. Like neuroscientists who use fMRI(功育磁共振成像）scanning to determine how regions in the brain respond to different stimuli, Cole and Fredrickson are interested in how the body, at the genetic level, responds to feelings of happiness and meaning.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 在注意到每个受试者的意义和幸福感后，弗雷德里克森和科尔与他们的研究同事一起研究了每个参与者中某些基因表达的方式。就像神经科学家使用功能磁共振成像扫描来确定大脑区域如何对不同刺激做出反应一样，科尔和弗雷德里克森对身体在基因水平上如何对幸福感和意义感做出反应感兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Cole’s past work has linked various kinds of chronic adversity to a particular gene expression pattern. When people feel lonely, are grieving the loss of a loved one, or are struggling to make ends meet, their bodies go into threat mode. This triggers the activation of a stress-related gene pattern that has two features ： an increase in the activity of pro-inflammatory(促炎症的)genes and a decrease in the activity of genes involved in anti-viral responses.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 科尔过去的工作将各种慢性逆境与特定的基因表达模式联系起来。当人们感到孤独、因失去亲人而悲伤或难以维持收支平衡时，他们的身体就会进入威胁模式。这会触发与压力相关的基因模式的激活，该模式具有两个特征：促炎基因活性增加和参与抗病毒反应的基因活性降低。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Cole and Fredrickson found that people who are happy but have little to no sense of meaning in their lives have the same gene expression patterns as people who are responding to and enduring chronic adversity. That is, the bodies of these happy people are preparing them for bacterial threats by activating the pro-inflammatory response. Chronic inflammation is, of course, associated with major illnesses like heart disease and various cancers.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 科尔和弗雷德里克森发现，那些快乐但几乎没有生活意义的人与那些应对和忍受长期逆境的人具有相同的基因表达模式。也就是说，这些快乐的人的身体正在通过激活促炎症反应来为细菌威胁做好准备。当然，慢性炎症与心脏病和各种癌症等重大疾病有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) “Empty positive emotions”-like the kind people experience during manic (狂喜的）episodes or artificially induced euphoria (欣快）from alcohol and drugs—“are about as good for you as adversity，” says Fredrickson.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）“空虚的积极情绪”——就像人们在狂喜的时候所经历的那种情绪，或者由于酒精和毒品而人为诱发的欣快感——“对你来说和逆境一样有好处，”弗雷德里克森说。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) It’s important to understand that for many people, a sense of meaning and happiness in life overlap；many people score jointly high (or jointly low) on the happiness and meaning measures in the study. But for many others, there is a dissonance (不一致）-they feel that they are low on happiness and high on meaning or that their lives are very high in happiness, but low in meaning. This last group, which has the gene expression pattern associated with adversity, formed 75 percent of study participants. Only one quarter of the study participants had what the researchers call “eudaimonic predominance”-that is, their sense of meaning outpaced their feelings of happiness.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 重要的是要明白，对于许多人来说，生活的意义感和幸福感是重叠的；在研究中，许多人在幸福感和意义测量上得分共同高（或共同低）。但对于其他许多人来说，存在一种不和谐（不一致）——他们觉得自己幸福感低而意义感高，或者他们的生活幸福感很高，但意义却很低。最后一组具有与逆境相关的基因表达模式，占研究参与者的75%。只有四分之一的研究参与者具有研究人员所说的“eudaimonic predominance”——也就是说，他们的意义感超过了他们的幸福感。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) This is too bad given the more beneficial gene expression pattern associated with meaningfulness. People whose levels of happiness and meaning line up, and people who have a strong sense of meaning but are not necessarily happy, showed a de-activation of the adversity stress response. Their bodies were not preparing them for the bacterial infections that we get when we are alone or in trouble, but for the viral infections we get when surrounded by a lot of other people.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 考虑到与意义相关的更有益的基因表达模式，这太糟糕了。幸福感和意义感一致的人，以及具有强烈意义感但不一定幸福的人，表现出逆境压力反应的失活。他们的身体并没有为我们独自一人或遇到麻烦时感染的细菌做好准备，而是为我们被很多其他人包围时感染的病毒做好准备。

paragraphs.sourceText: P) Fredrickson’s past research, described in her two books, Positivity and Love 2.0, has mapped the benefits of positive emotions in individuals. She has found that positive emotions broaden a person’s perspective and help protect people against adversity. So it was surprising to her that hedonic wellbeing, which is associated with positive emotions and pleasure, did so badly in this study compared with eudaimonic well-being. Q) “It’s not the amount of hedonic happiness that’s a problem.” Fredrickson tells me, “It’s that it’s not matched by eudaimonic well-being. It’s great when both are in step. But if you have more hedonic well-being than would be expected, that’s when this [gene] pattern that’s similar to adversity emerged. ” R) The terms hedonism and eudaimonism bring to mind the great philosophical debate, which has shaped Western civilization for over 2 000 years, about the nature of the good life. Does happiness lie in feeling good, as hedonists think, or in doing and being good, as Aristotle and his intellectual descendants, the ethicists(伦理学家），think? From the evidence of this study, it seems that feeling good is not enough. People need meaning to thrive. In the words of Carl Jung, “The least of things with a meaning is worth more in life than the greatest of things without it.” Jung’s wisdom certainly seems to apply to our bodies, if not also to our hearts and our minds. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: P) Fredrickson 过去的研究在她的两本书《Positivity and Love 2.0》中进行了描述，描绘了积极情绪对个人的好处。她发现积极的情绪可以拓宽一个人的视野，并有助于保护人们免受逆境的影响。因此，令她惊讶的是，与积极情绪和快乐相关的享乐幸福感在这项研究中与幸福感相比表现得如此糟糕。问）“问题不在于享乐幸福的多少。”弗雷德里克森告诉我，“问题在于它与幸福感不匹配。两者步调一致固然很棒。但如果你的享乐幸福感超出预期，那么这种类似于逆境的[基因]模式就会出现。”R) 享乐主义和幸福主义这两个术语让人想起关于幸福本质的伟大哲学辩论，这场辩论塑造了西方文明 2000 多年的历史。美好的生活。幸福是像享乐主义者所认为的那样，在于感觉良好，还是像亚里士多德和他的思想后裔、伦理学家（伦理学家）所认为的那样，在于做事和做好事？从这项研究的证据来看，感觉良好似乎还不够。人们需要意义才能茁壮成长。用卡尔·荣格的话来说，“在生活中，具有意义的最小的事物比没有意义的最伟大的事物更有价值。”荣格的智慧似乎当然适用于我们的身体，如果不是也适用于我们的心灵和思想。注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2上作答。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. The author’s recent article examined how a meaningful life is different from a happy life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 作者最近的文章探讨了有意义的生活与幸福的生活有何不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. It should be noted that many people feel their life is both happy and meaningful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 值得注意的是，许多人觉得自己的生活既幸福又有意义。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. According to one survey, there is a close relationship between hedonic well-being measures and high scores on happiness.

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. According to one of the authors of a new study, what makes life meaningful may not make people happy.

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Experiments were carried out to determine our body’s genetic expression of feelings of happiness and meaning.

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. A new study claims happiness may not contribute to health.

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. Evidence from research shows that it takes meaning for people to thrive.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 研究证据表明，人们的成长需要意义。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. With regard to gene expression patterns, happy people with little or no sense of meaning in life are found to be similar to those suffering from chronic adversity.

paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 当今大多数关于幸福的书籍都声称幸福有益于健康。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Nothing succeeds in business books like the study of success. The current business-book boom was launched in 1982 by Tom Peters and Robert Waterman with In Search of Excellence. The trend has continued with a succession of experts and would-be experts who promise to distil the essence of excellence into three (or five or seven) simple rules.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在商业书籍中，没有什么比对成功的研究更成功的了。当前的商业书籍热潮始于 1982 年汤姆·彼得斯 (Tom Peters) 和罗伯特·沃特曼 (Robert Waterman) 的《追求卓越》(In Search of Excellence)。这一趋势仍在继续，一系列专家和未来的专家承诺将卓越的本质提炼成三个（或五个或七个）简单的规则。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Three Rules is a self-conscious contribution to this type of writing；it even includes a bibliography of “success studies”. Michael Raynor and Mumtaz Ahmed work for a consultancy, Deloitte, that is determined to turn itself into more of a thought-leader and less a corporate repairman. They employ all the tricks of the success books. They insist that their conclusions are “measurable and actionable”-guides to behaviour rather than analysis for its own sake. Success authors usually serve up vivid stories about how exceptional businesspeople stamped their personalities on a company or rescued it from a life-threatening crisis. Messrs Raynor and Ahmed are happier chewing the numbers：they provide detailed appendices on “calculating the elements of advantage” and “detailed analysis”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 《三法则》是对此类写作的自觉贡献，甚至包括“成功研究”的参考书目。迈克尔·雷诺 (Michael Raynor) 和穆塔兹·艾哈迈德 (Mumtaz Ahmed) 在德勤咨询公司工作，该公司决心将自己转变为思想领袖，而不是企业修理工。他们运用了成功书籍中的所有技巧。他们坚持认为他们的结论是“可衡量和可操作的”——是行为指南，而不是为了分析本身而进行的分析。成功作家通常会讲述一些生动的故事，讲述杰出的商人如何将自己的个性烙印在公司上，或将公司从危及生命的危机中拯救出来。雷诺和艾哈迈德先生更乐意咀嚼这些数字：他们提供了关于“计算优势要素”和“详细分析”的详细附录。

paragraphs.sourceText: The authors spent five years studying the behaviour of their 344 “ exceptional companies” only to come up at first with nothing. Every hunch (直觉) led to a blind alley and every hypothesis to a dead end. It was only when they shifted their attention from how companies behave to how they think that they began to make sense of their voluminous material.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作者花了五年时间研究 344 家“杰出公司”的行为，但一开始却一无所获。每一个直觉都通向死胡同，每一个假设都通向死胡同。只有当他们将注意力从公司的行为方式转移到他们的想法时，他们才开始理解他们的大量材料。

paragraphs.sourceText: Management is all about making difficult tradeoffs in conditions that are always uncertain and often fast-changing. But exceptional companies approach these tradeoffs with two simple rules in mind, sometimes consciously, sometimes unconsciously. First：better before cheaper. Companies are more likely to succeed in the long run if they compete on quality or performance than on price. Second：revenue before cost. Companies have more to gain in the long run from driving up revenue than by driving down costs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 管理就是在总是不确定且经常快速变化的条件下做出艰难的权衡。但杰出的公司在进行这些权衡时会牢记两个简单的规则，有时是有意识的，有时是无意识的。第一：更好先于更便宜。从长远来看，如果公司在质量或性能上竞争而不是在价格上竞争，那么他们更有可能取得成功。第二：成本前收入。从长远来看，公司从增加收入中获得的收益比从降低成本中获得的收益更多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most success studies suffer from two faults. There is “the halo ( 光环）effect”, whereby good performance leads commentators to attribute all manner of virtues to anything and everything the company does. These virtues then suddenly become vices when the company fails. Messrs Raynor and Ahmed work hard to avoid these mistakes by studying large bodies of data over several decades. But they end up embracing a different error：stating the obvious. Most businesspeople will not be surprised to learn that it is better to find a profitable niche(隙缝市场）and focus on boosting your revenues than to compete on price and cut your way to success. The difficult question is how to find that profitable niche and protect it. There, The Three Rules is less useful. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数成功研究都有两个缺陷。存在“光环效应”，良好的业绩导致评论者将公司所做的一切都归为美德。当公司失败时，这些美德突然变成了恶习。雷诺和艾哈迈德先生通过研究数十年的大量数据，努力避免这些错误。但他们最终却犯了一个不同的错误：陈述显而易见的事实。大多数商人不会感到惊讶，因为他们知道最好找到一个有利可图的利基市场（缝隙市场）并专注于增加你的收入，而不是在价格上竞争并削减你的成功之路，困难的问题是如何找到有利可图的利基市场并保护它，这三个规则就没那么有用了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Until recently, the University of Kent prided itself on its friendly image. Not any more. Over the past few months it has been working hard, with the help of media consultants, to play down its cosy reputation in favour of something more academic and serious.
paragraphs.translationZh: 直到最近，肯特大学还以其友好的形象而自豪。不再。在过去的几个月里，在媒体顾问的帮助下，它一直在努力淡化其舒适的声誉，转而支持更加学术和严肃的事物。

paragraphs.sourceText: Kent is not alone in considering an image revamp (翻新）,Changes to next year’s funding regime are forcing universities to justify charging students up to £9 000 in fees.
paragraphs.translationZh: 肯特郡并不是唯一一个考虑进行形象改造的人，明年资助制度的变化正迫使大学证明向学生收取高达 9000 英镑的费用是合理的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Nowadays universities are putting much more of a focus on their brands and what their value propositions are. While in the past universities have often focused on student social life and attractions of the university town in recruitment campaigns, they are now concentrating on more tangible (实在的）attractions, such as employment prospects, engagement with industry, and lecturer contact hours, making clear exactly what students are going to get for their money.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如今，大学更加关注其品牌及其价值主张。过去，大学在招聘活动中经常关注学生的社交生活和大学城的景点，但现在他们专注于更切实的景点，例如就业前景、与行业的接触以及讲师的接触时间，明确学生将通过他们的钱得到什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: The problem for universities is that if those benefits fail to materialise, students notice. That worries Rob Behrens, who deals with student complaints. “Universities need to be extremely careful in describing what’s going to happen to students，” he says. “As competition is going to get greater for attracting gifted students, there is a danger that universities will go the extra mile.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学面临的问题是，如果这些好处未能实现，学生们就会注意到。这让负责处理学生投诉的罗布·贝伦斯 (Rob Behrens) 感到担忧。 “大学在描述学生将会发生的事情时需要非常小心，”他说。 “随着吸引天才学生的竞争变得更加激烈，大学可能会付出更多的努力。

paragraphs.sourceText: One university told prospective engineering students they would be able to design a car and race it at Brands Hatch, which never happened, he says. Others have promised use of sophisticated equipment that turned out to be broken or unavailable. “If universities spent as much money on handling complaints and appeals appropriately as they spend on marketing, they would do better at keeping students, and in the National Student Survey returns，” he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他说，一所大学告诉未来的工程专业学生，他们将能够设计一辆汽车并在布兰兹哈奇进行比赛，但这从未发生过。其他人承诺使用复杂的设备，但结果证明这些设备已损坏或无法使用。他说：“如果大学在妥善处理投诉和上诉方面投入的资金与在营销方面投入的资金一样多，那么它们在留住学生方面会做得更好，在全国学生调查结果中也会更好。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Ongoing research tracking prospective 2012 students suggests that they are not only becoming more sophisticated in thinking about what they want from a university, but are also spending more time researching evidence to back up institutional claims.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正在进行的对 2012 届学生的跟踪研究表明，他们不仅在思考自己想从大学得到什么方面变得更加成熟，而且还花更多的时间研究证据来支持机构的主张。

paragraphs.sourceText: Hence the growing importance of the student survey. From next September, all institutions will also be expected to publish on their websites key information sets, allowing easier comparison between institutions, between promises and reality, and the types of jobs and salaries graduates go on to.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，学生调查的重要性日益增加。从明年 9 月开始，所有院校也将在其网站上发布关键信息集，以便更容易地比较院校之间、承诺与现实以及毕业生继续从事的工作类型和薪资。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a result, it is hardly surprising that universities are beginning to change the way they market themselves. While the best form of marketing for institutions is to be good at what they do, they also need to be clear about how they are different from others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，大学开始改变自己的营销方式也就不足为奇了。虽然机构的最佳营销形式是擅长自己所做的事情，但他们也需要清楚自己与其他机构的不同之处。

paragraphs.sourceText: And it is vital that once an institution claims to be particularly good at something, it must live up to it. The moment you position yourself, you become exposed, and if you fail in that you are in trouble. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 至关重要的是，一旦一个机构声称自己特别擅长某件事，它就必须做到这一点。一旦你定位自己，你就暴露了，如果你失败了，你就有麻烦了。
